full_details: At Paul's you meant to check Daniel, and the line stood as your own copy had it. A thin new book stopped you. You read the epistle standing. You bought it for sixpence and said nothing. At home you copied one sentence and ruled a line under it, and wrote no answer. At the Theatre the share was forty shillings, against eight-and-twenty last Saturday, the spring's best. The chest was not counted. The sheet was the share, not the lease. After supper you sat. The landing and the greeting were already done. The speech came whole. You did not walk it. Then Flint, and a king coming down. At one you refused the boast, and you slept at home.
one_sentence: You bought a thin book for sixpence, took forty shillings, and sat to write the death of kings.
title: Sixpence, forty shillings, and the speech written sitting
